title: Ukraine strikes Berdiansk and Luhansk airfields in reported first use of ATACMS
body:
In the early hours of 17 October 2023, Ukraine struck Russian-occupied airfields near Berdiansk and Luhansk. Kyiv Post reported explosions shortly after 2:30 a.m. and said the reported targets at Berdiansk were helicopters, an artillery system and an ammunition warehouse. Ka-52, Mi-8, Mi-24 and Mi-28 helicopters were reportedly based there.

The Ukrainian military initially said at least two Russian helicopters on the ground at Berdiansk had been destroyed, along with an artillery system and an ammunition warehouse. Kyiv later claimed nine helicopters destroyed, along with an air defence launcher and an ammunition warehouse, and said runways were damaged. Official Ukrainian statements spoke of successful strikes on helicopters and airfield equipment in occupied Luhansk and Berdiansk but did not name the weapon used. President Volodymyr Zelensky thanked those destroying the occupiers' logistics bases.

A Wall Street Journal report, added to the Kyiv Post article as an update, said the attack used ATACMS missiles. A pro-Russian Telegram channel also claimed ATACMS were used. The Berdiansk occupation authority claimed all incoming weapons were intercepted. Kyiv Post said that officially Ukraine did not then have any ATACMS and that Washington had been slow to approve a transfer after repeated Ukrainian requests. The article gave the missile's range as up to about 500 kilometres.
